habitats: Coastal spray belt above mean high tide
Sea-arch and islet margins above regular inundation
summary: A sprawling evergreen succulent shrub, 0.3–1.2 m tall, with salt-secreting leaves and woody runners rooting at sediment-covered nodes. It occupies drained spray-zone ground above recurring spring-tide inundation and ordinary wave runup, offering limited low shade. Salt crusts are harvestable mainly after dry weather; fog redissolves them and rain can wash them away. Exceptional storm washover can kill patches (F13, F19, F20, F23).

links: Marine spray loads foliage and rooting ground with salt.
Ion compartmentation and gland secretion control internal salt concentrations; the plant's benefit is ion balance.
Fleshy leaves store water obtained through roots, while sufficiently dry afternoons or dry spells let secreted droplets form crusts on exposed margins.
Fog and humid conditions redissolve crusts into brine, and rain can wash the salt away; creatures harvest a secretion byproduct rather than a plant-provided food reward.
chains.play: Collect leaf-margin salt after dry weather and watch for coloso taking surface salt without assuming foliage browsing.
chains.weakness: Salt secretion costs water and energy; humid weather limits dry yield, rain removes salt, and prolonged flooding or exceptional storm washover can kill patches.
observe: Exposed margins develop white crusts after a dry afternoon.
Fog turns crusts into droplets; rain washes salt away while leaves remain firm.
Coloso occasionally licks accessible leaf-surface salt.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Rooting sites remain above mean high tide in the spray belt. Salt tolerance does not confer regular submergence tolerance; salt is a mineral reward rather than an alkaloid defence. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: Collectible crystals were treated as the default, so salt harvest is now conditional on dry weather and secretion is identified as ion regulation rather than a food reward. Still open: The ion-regulation mechanism is credible, and F20 and F23 support marine salt exposure and creature salt collection. The weather-to-crust link is insufficiently specified: F15's humid climate does not mean every humid interval redissolves crystals. Deliquescence depends on salt composition, temperature and a humidity threshold; actual fog wetting can dissolve deposits directly. As written, the chain and generator can remove harvestable crust whenever air is labelled humid, including conditions in which crystals would persist.

analogues.organism: Salt-excreting Limonium species and succulent coastal halophytes
analogues.mechanism: Ion compartmentation, gland secretion and water storage support saline terrestrial life; dry surface deposits depend on local humidity and evaporation and do not imply a feeding mutualism.

chains.trait: Low woody runners rooting at sediment-covered nodes
links: Dense-air winds impose strong loads on coastal shoots.
Low crowns shorten the lever arm through which wind bends stems, even where sprawling plants occupy a broad ground area.
Surface runners form adventitious roots where shallow sediment covers nodes and roots reach stable substrate.
Distributed anchorage supports overlapping low branches that provide limited visual concealment and shade.
chains.play: Use mature crowns for low visual cover and limited shade where body size and canopy density permit.
chains.weakness: Unburied nodes provide no additional root anchorage; scour can undermine rooted pockets, and low crowns conceal only suitably small bodies.
observe: Seaward branches lie lower than sheltered shoots.
Sediment-covered runner nodes carry roots into stable ground.
Small zancuda use overlapping branches as visual cover above their tidal feeding grounds.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Low geometry and distributed anchorage reduce wind damage without preventing storm losses. Shade does not erase scent trails. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: The chain confused spreading area with reduced wind loading and assumed every node was buried, so it now specifies short leverage and conditional rooting at sediment-covered nodes. Residual: F4 and F19 support increased aerodynamic loading at a given wind speed. Lower crowns shorten bending leverage without necessarily reducing projected area, and rooted nodes can distribute anchorage. Residual weakness: this benefit depends on substrate resistance and actual root establishment; a connected mat over loose sediment can fail collectively. The revision requires stable rooting pockets and acknowledges scour mortality. Concealment remains conditional on creature size rather than being established for every zancuda.

analogues.mechanism: Low height shortens bending leverage, flexible shoots reconfigure under wind, and runners gain distributed anchorage where covered nodes root into stable substrate.

food_for: Player lineage collecting salt; foliage consumption is not established
gameplay.gift_item: Dry leaf-margin salt crust for a receptive salt-seeking creature

poison.signal: Glaucous green leaves with salt droplets or dry white crusts; no red-veined alkaloid warning, but colour does not establish edibility and excessive salt intake is hazardous.

gameplay.cover: Limited low visual cover and shade beneath overlapping crowns; useful only where body size and canopy density permit.
gameplay.nest_material: Dry fine twigs above the storm-wrack line.
gameplay.mineral_lick: Leaf and stem salt crusts chiefly after dry weather; fog redissolves them and rain can wash them away.
gameplay.notes: Salt collection does not establish foliage edibility or a benefit to the plant. Salt load limits consumption. Root water is still necessary despite succulence. Recurring tidal inundation and ordinary wave runup exclude establishment; exceptional storm washover remains a mortality event.

relations.note: Occasionally takes accessible leaf-surface salt; routine low shoot browsing is not assumed.
Dense overlapping branches conceal suitably small individuals above tidal feeding grounds.
Occupies the terrestrial spray belt above the regularly flooded algal zone rather than sharing its inundated substrate.

generator.trunk: Several short woody bases connected by surface runners; nodes root where shallow accumulated sediment covers them.

branching.buttress: None; sediment-covered nodes form adventitious roots where stable substrate is available.

overlay_rules: White crystals accumulate at gland-bearing margins only under sufficiently dry conditions.
Fog and humid air can redissolve crusts into clear salt droplets.
Rain washes salt away without inherently changing living leaf colour.

placement.slope: Stable sediment pockets on 0–35 degree coastal slopes; exclude active scour.
placement.wetness: Drained spray-zone ground outside modeled recurring spring-high-water inundation and ordinary wave runup; allow only exceptional storm washover.
placement.soil: Rock fissures, coarse sand and sediment pockets without active geothermal contamination; anchoring roots must reach stable substrate.
placement.fog: Tolerates marine fog; fog redissolves dry salt deposits and does not guarantee root water.
placement.density: Irregular sprawling patches filtered by local tidal inundation, wave exposure and stable rooting pockets.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen; grows after sustained rain. Salt crusts develop during sufficiently dry intervals. Winter storms remove tips and can kill washed-over patches.
generator.wind_response: Outer shoots flex near the ground; low height shortens bending leverage. Crowns become asymmetric toward shelter, with reduced exposed-side height but no assumed reduction in total projected area.

journal.en: The bush leaves salt on its lips. Beneath it, even the pale ones can rest.
journal.es: El arbusto deja sal en sus labios. Debajo, hasta los pálidos pueden descansar.

changelog.what: flora pass: 7 voices drafted and peer-reviewed, Composer botanical referee, sol chaired and applied the fixes

strict second review (sol + DeepSeek) applied by sol: Replaced mean-high-tide placement with a local spring-tide and ordinary-wave inundation mask consistent with F13; exceptional storms can still kill plants.; Separated salt collection from unsupported succulent browsing and removed generic foliage-consumer claims.; Removed albino shelter because exposed low coastal crowns do not establish the shaded refuge its lore requires.

observe: White-rimmed shrubs grow above the regularly wetted shore.
Washed outer leaves lack crystals retained inside the crown.
Rooted runners connect apparently separate crowns.
secrets: Inner leaves can retain crystals after a light shower.
Repeated browsing reveals a coastal mineral route used by coloso.
